result:
I’d make it impossible for anyone to cause harm they don’t fully feel.

No distance, no abstraction, no rationalization. If you bomb a city, you’d feel the heat of it. If you defraud a pensioner, you’d feel the panic of an empty account. If you dump poison in a river, you’d taste it in every downstream glass. The consequences of your actions would land on your own nervous system with the same force they land on others.

Not a moral rule. Not a law. Just a change in how human brains are wired—so that empathy stops being a choice and becomes a physiological inevitability.

This would end most wars, most exploitation, most environmental destruction. People would still be free to do terrible things, but only in the way they’re free to touch a hot stove. Nobody would do it twice.

I know the cost: we’d lose some of the brutal efficiency that built modern civilization—the ability to forget, to buy cheap goods made by suffering hands, to stand on the shoulders of misery without noticing. But we’d gain something the species has never once experienced: a civilization that can’t lie to itself about what it does. And that seems worth more than everything we’d have to give up.
